The covering test, "worker claim race: two dispatches of one turn produce one completed turn and one proposal set" (src/lib/agents/operator/__tests__/turn-worker.integration.test.ts:319), still PASSED. A confirming run of the whole agent-turn test set under the same mutant — turn-worker.integration.test.ts + worker/jobs/agent-turn/__tests__ + turns.test.ts — reported 23 passed, 0 failed. The behavioural replacement: the concurrent section of that test (turn-worker.integration.test.ts:500-517) should assert that exactly one attempt reached the model and was billed (expect(runLlmTask).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) and one recordApiCost / api_costs row for the racy turn), and a direct claimTurn case should prove a second claim inside the lease returns null while one after lease expiry succeeds.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Round 2 re-derived this disposition from evidence produced in this pass at head 3a377f6562ce564051b7fd21bd751c9bd9be49ed; the round-1 arbiter reasoning is retained below and was not re-used as proof. || Not an equivalent mutation. Deleting the lease predicate lets a second dispatch claim a turn whose 180 s lease is live (AGENT_TURN_LEASE_SECONDS, worker/jobs/agent-turn/constants.ts), so two attempts each run step 3, each build a snapshot and each make their own cost-guarded owner_operator model call. The intake's own risk_reasons names this consequence verbatim: "a new BullMQ worker (AgentTurnWorker) makes a cost-guarded LLM call ... a defect can double-bill or strand turns". Not an unexecuted branch either: the test's third section runs two handleAgentTurn calls under Promise.all on one freshly created turn, so both reach claimTurn inside the same lease window, and claimTurn is the first statement either executes after the flag gate. It survives because the assertions describe only the END STATE — one completed turn, one agent_proposals row, outbox completed — and completeTurnFenced's attempt_token fence delivers that end state on its own, independently of the lease. The lease predicate and the completion fence are two separate guards: the fence stops a stale attempt from WRITING, only the lease stops a second attempt from SPENDING. The suite asserts the first and never the second. Independently corroborated without spending a further run: "rg AGENT_TURN_LEASE_SECONDS|leaseSeconds|LEASE" across src/lib/agents/operator/__tests__ and worker/jobs/agent-turn/__tests__ returns no hit, the only two claimed_at writes in the suite (turn-worker.integration.test.ts:549, :585) drive loadPredecessor's age rather than the claim, and the claim-race test makes no runLlmTask or recordApiCost call-count assertion at all. Mutation t-m2, which removed completeTurnFenced's attempt_token fence, was KILLED — so the pair is asymmetric: the written-state half of the protocol is asserted and the spend half is not.
